thread:
maria (PM): Quick sync — need to finalize v2 route compatibility tradeoffs and deprecation timeline. Customers asking for function-calls parity, embeddings naming, and rerank behavior. Can we decide today?

jake (Eng Runtime): function-calls parity is non-trivial — v2 changed the callback contract. We can add a shim to translate v1 calls to v2 but it adds ~2-3ms/req and more code surface.

anita (Product Eng): Key ask from Acme & FinCo: identical tool-calling contract or they refuse to migrate. We should split must-haves vs nice-to-haves.

maria (PM): Proposal: Must-have = same request/response keys for chat+function_call, stable embeddings vector shape, rerank endpoint accepts same input ordering. Nice-to-have = verbatim response headers + legacy error codes.

jake (Eng Runtime): embeddings vector shape is fine. Rerank: v2 sorts by score desc by default; v1 used a deterministic tie-breaker by id. We can emulate tie-breaker behind an opt-in flag `tie_break=v1`.

suresh (SRE): Ops note: the shim increases p99 latency by ~5% at peak in our stress runs. If enabled globally we'll need to reserve extra capacity. Suggest canary on Dedicated + Hosted subset first.

deploy-bot (bot): canary deployment started for branch api/v2-compat-bridge on infra-dedicated-3

olivia (Developer): For migration guide include code diffs and quick SDK patches. Example snippet: 
```
// v1
POST /v1/chat
body: {messages, max_tokens}
// v2
POST /v2/chat/completions
body: {instances: [{messages}], completion_options}
```

anita (Product Eng): Draft launch criteria: 
- shim implements function_call parity across common models
- embeddings regression tests (dim + normalization) pass
- rerank backward-compat opt-in flag exists and documented
- migration guide + 3 sample SDK patches (python/js/go)
- canary workflow: 1% -> 10% -> 100% with zero user-facing regressions

maria (PM): Deprecation timeline suggestion: announce 6 months before; maintain v1 for 9 months; start redirect/encouragement at 6 months; full shutdown at 12 months. Thoughts?

jake (Eng Runtime): 12 months is tight if shim continues to be maintained. Can we aim for customers to move in 9 months and then retire shim 3 months later?

suresh (SRE): Ops prefers staged reduction: shim on for all Hosted for initial 3 months post-launch, then Hosted-only for next 6 months, Dedicated customers get extended window via contract/extension. That reduces blast radius.

maria (PM): Action items:
- @jake prototype shim + perf numbers by EOD Fri
- @anita draft migration guide and SDK snippets by Tue
- @suresh canary rollout plan & capacity numbers by Mon
- @olivia create examples repo + CT tests

jake (Eng Runtime): noted. I'll post perf microbenchmarks here when ready :eyes: 

olivia (Developer): i'll start the examples repo, can pair with @anita tomorrow morning

maria (PM): Thanks all. Reconvene Thu 10am to lock timeline. :thumbsup:
